Definition: Percentage of individuals who used the internet (from any location, via any device) in the last three months. This measures actual internet adoption beyond network availability, capturing the combined effect of infrastructure, affordability, digital literacy, and relevance.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed: ITU DataHub and World Bank/FRED both report 20.5% of individuals using the internet in Mozambique for 2024, matching the original Wikipedia-cited figure. Code 2 (15-29%) is correct; original source was weak (aggregator) but the figure is corroborated by primary ITU/World Bank data.

Definition: Whether the country has an operational Internet Exchange Point (IXP) and its maturity. IXPs enable local internet traffic to be exchanged domestically rather than being routed internationally, reducing latency, costs, and dependence on foreign infrastructure. Critical for local digital ecosystem development.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed via Capacity Media (May 2025) and PeeringDB/Internet Society Pulse: MOZIX is Mozambique's sole IXP, with around 19 peering members and over 150 Gbps peak traffic. This supports 'active IXP with moderate participation' (code 4); original single datacentermap.com source is corroborated.

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: DataReportal/GSMA Intelligence confirm 18.91 million mobile connections in Mozambique at start-2024, equivalent to 55.0% of population — but this is a 'connections' figure (SIM-based, can include multi-SIM users), not the 'unique subscriber' metric the variable requires. GSMA unique-subscriber penetration is typically materially lower than connections and could fall in the 40-54% band instead. Could not source GSMA's unique-subscriber figure directly before research access was exhausted. Left unchanged but flagged for human review to confirm against GSMA Intelligence unique subscriber data specifically.

Definition: The availability and presence of major cloud service providers (hyperscale and regional) operating in or serving the country with local or near-local infrastructure. Cloud availability determines access to scalable computing resources for government, business, and startups.
Value Name: Served remotely from distant regions only (>100ms latency)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original code 2 is out of date and the cited afribit.co.za blog is a weak, tangential source about Google Cloud's broader African expansion, not Mozambique-specific. DataCenterDynamics (2026) reports BCX has launched Alibaba Cloud's Africa Local Public Cloud service hosted in a Maputo data centre, giving Mozambique a local hyperscale-affiliated cloud presence. Revised to code 4 (at least one major provider with local presence).

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Legislation enacted but no enforcement authority
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original code 3 (enacted, no enforcement) is incorrect: Mozambique has no comprehensive data protection act in force. A draft Personal Data Protection Law went to public consultation (INTIC, Sept 2025) and was approved as a bill by the Council of Ministers in March 2026, but has not yet been passed by the Assembleia da República. Only partial provisions exist via the 2017 Electronic Transactions Law and the ratified AU Malabo Convention. Revised to code 2 (draft legislation/partial provisions in other laws).

Comments: Vodacom Tier III data center, 4 colocation facilities

revision_notes: Corroborated and upgraded: Inflect's directory (September 2025) lists at least seven Maputo facilities including a Digital Realty carrier-neutral site (MPM1), NTT, SEACOM, PCCW Global and Teledata, in addition to the previously noted Vodacom Tier III facility. This constitutes multiple Tier III-class facilities from reputable operators, meeting code 4 rather than the originally recorded code 3.

Definition: Whether the government has established dedicated data center infrastructure and/or a government cloud (G-Cloud) strategy for hosting e-government services and public sector data domestically. Critical for data sovereignty and e-government service delivery.
Value Name: Government data center planned or under construction
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original code 2 (planned/under construction) understates status: the government's primary data centre at the Parque de Ciência e Tecnologia de Maluana (built under the MEGCIP project) is already operational, though under-utilised, per the World Bank's Digital Acceleration Project appraisal document (2022). A National Digital Transformation Strategy was only launched for drafting in February 2026 and is not yet adopted. This matches code 3 (basic government data centre operational, no adopted cloud strategy yet) rather than code 2 or 4.

Definition: Percentage of national population with access to electricity (grid or off-grid). This is the primary indicator of energy infrastructure availability for ICT. Based on World Bank/IEA Tracking SDG7 data, national statistical offices, or Afrobarometer surveys.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original code 4 (75-89%) is far too high and even contradicts the row's own comment (60%). World Bank/ESMAP Tracking SDG7 data (the primary source specified in the guidelines) records access to electricity in Mozambique at 36.0% in 2023, placing the country in the 25-49% band (code 2). Note: IEA's Mozambique 2024 report cites a higher 48% figure for 2022 — this discrepancy between sources should be checked by a human reviewer, but the WB/ESMAP figure is used here as the guideline-specified primary source.

redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed: RISE (ESMAP/World Bank) scores Mozambique's off-grid systems framework highly, and FUNAE operates around 76 mini-grids (~6MW) under an active off-grid regulation, per the AfDB 2021 sector diagnostic. Code 3 (active policy, some deployment) holds; original tandfonline source is corroborated by more authoritative regulatory data.

Definition: Percentage of total electricity generation from renewable sources (hydro, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass). Indicates energy sustainability and potential for distributed power solutions relevant to ICT infrastructure in off-grid areas.

revision_notes: Confirmed but re-sourced: the original citation was a 2010 IRENA country profile, 15 years out of date. The IEA's Mozambique 2024 report confirms electricity generation remains dominated by hydropower (83%), with gas (15%) and coal (0.1%) making up the balance, keeping the renewable generation share well within the 75%+ band (code 5).

Definition: The maturity of the country's technology startup ecosystem, based on the number of tech startups, venture capital activity, accelerators/incubators, and the presence of a supportive ecosystem. Africa's startup scene is well-documented by trackers like Partech, Disrupt Africa, and Briter Bridges.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Dealroom's Mozambique ecosystem profile shows $0 VC invested in the last 12 months, only 9 tracked startups and a combined enterprise value of $20M (ranked 36th of tracked African ecosystems), indicating negligible disclosed VC activity. This is closer to 'Nascent' (code 1) than the previously recorded 'Emerging' (code 2); Partech's 2025 Africa report, the original source, does not mention Mozambique among funded markets at all, consistent with very limited activity. Flagged as a judgement call given thin data coverage — recommend human review.

redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source (a GSMA blog citing a continent-wide count of 618 active hubs) was not Mozambique-specific and did not actually support a country score. AfriLabs' directory identifies at least three active Mozambican hubs/incubators (Iniciativa para Democracia e Cidadania, ideiaLab Mozambique, Ideario Hub), and ANDE's 2025 ecosystem map indicates further support organisations. This places Mozambique at the low end of code 3 (3-9 hubs) rather than code 2, though activity levels are not independently confirmed — recommend human review to verify activity levels.

Measured through proxies such as GitHub activity, Stack Overflow representation, local tech meetup groups, and developer surveys. Value Name: Emerging (small but growing community, <1,000 active developers)

revision_notes: MozDevz, Mozambique's main developer community, reports over 2,000 active community members and 600+ trained talents (mozdevz.org, accessed 2026), exceeding the <1,000 threshold used for 'Emerging' (code 2). Revised to code 3 (Developing, 1,000-10,000 developers), noting this is a single community's self-reported figure rather than an independent census — some human verification recommended.

The previously recorded EGDI of 0.313 (2022, Middle band, code 2) is plausible for a low-income country but is unconfirmed for the 2024 survey round. Definition: The scale and quality of tertiary-level ICT and STEM education programmes available in the country, based on the number and quality of institutions offering ICT degrees, computer science programmes, and engineering courses relative to the population.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original source (a UNESCO regional office landing page) was not substantively about tertiary STEM education. Better evidence: WIPO's GII 2024 country profile shows gross tertiary enrolment of only 7.3% and science/engineering graduates at 9.6% of the total (global rank 111/133); UNCTAD (2024) notes 56 HEIs exist nationally but ICT-specific programme depth remains limited, centred mainly on Eduardo Mondlane University. This supports 'Limited (few institutions, low enrolment)' — code 2 confirmed with stronger sourcing.
